body.name: Fighter Jet
body.h1: Fighter Jet Dot to Dot — 78 Dots for a High-Flying Adventure
body.tagline: Ready for Takeoff, Dot by Dot!
body.description: Connect 78 dots to reveal a sleek fighter jet soaring through the sky. This intermediate printable helps children practise number sequencing, concentration, visual tracking, and careful pencil control.
body.fun_fact: Fighter jets have swept-back wings that help them fly at very high speeds with less air resistance.

dot_guide.heading: How to Solve the Fighter Jet Dot-to-Dot Puzzle
dot_guide.intro: This speedy fighter jet is ready to zoom across the sky! The 78-dot challenge is divided into five clear stages for children comfortable with longer number sequences. Find dot 1 and get ready for takeoff!
dot_guide.outro: Amazing work—your fighter jet is ready to soar through the clouds! Colour it in bold blues and greys, then draw some fluffy clouds around it. Try the dinosaur dot to dot puzzles next for another exciting adventure.

sections.title: The Nose and Cockpit
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 16 to draw the pointed nose and the cockpit where the pilot sits.
sections.fact: The cockpit has a clear canopy so the pilot can see all around the sky while flying.

sections.title: The Sweeping Wings
sections.learn: Continue from dot 17 to dot 32 to shape the jet's long, sweeping wings.
sections.fact: Angled wings help a jet cut through the air smoothly and fly faster than planes with straight wings.

sections.title: The Body of the Jet
sections.learn: Follow dots 33 through 48 along the sleek body connecting the wings to the tail.
sections.fact: A jet's body is built from strong, lightweight materials so it can fly fast while staying sturdy.

sections.title: The Tail Fins
sections.learn: Trace dots 49 through 64 to add the tall tail fins that help the jet stay steady in flight.
sections.fact: Tail fins act like the fins on a fish, helping the jet balance and steer through the air.

sections.title: The Engines and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 65 through 78 to complete the powerful engines at the back of the jet.
sections.fact: Jet engines pull air in, heat it up, and push it out the back to create the thrust that sends the plane forward.

body.name: Private Jet
body.h1: Private Jet Dot to Dot — 66 Dots for a High-Flying Adventure
body.tagline: A Smooth Ride Through the Clouds!
body.description: Connect 66 dots to reveal a sleek private jet cruising through the sky. This easy, beginner-friendly printable helps children practise number sequencing, concentration, and steady pencil control.
body.fun_fact: Private jets are much smaller than the big airliners at the airport, and they're often used by families or businesspeople flying to places without a direct commercial flight.

dot_guide.heading: How to Solve the Private Jet Dot-to-Dot Puzzle
dot_guide.intro: This shiny private jet is ready for a smooth flight! The 66-dot challenge is divided into five easy stages, perfect for younger puzzlers. Find dot 1 and hop aboard!
dot_guide.outro: Wonderful flying—your private jet is ready for takeoff! Colour it in shiny whites and silvers, then add a sunny sky behind it. Try the fighter jet dot to dot puzzle next for a faster-paced challenge.

sections.title: The Nose and Cockpit
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 14 to draw the rounded nose and the cockpit windows up front.
sections.fact: The pilots sit right behind the cockpit windows so they can see the sky and runway clearly.

sections.title: The Slim Wings
sections.learn: Continue from dot 15 to dot 27 to shape the jet's slim, gently swept wings.
sections.fact: Private jets have smaller wings than airliners because they carry fewer passengers and less weight.

sections.title: The Cabin Windows
sections.learn: Follow dots 28 through 40 along the row of little windows on the body of the jet.
sections.fact: Inside, a private jet usually has comfy seats for just a handful of passengers instead of hundreds.

sections.title: The Tail Fin
sections.learn: Trace dots 41 through 53 to add the tall tail fin at the back of the jet.
sections.fact: The tail fin helps keep the jet flying straight and steady, just like the tail feathers on a bird.

sections.title: The Engines and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 54 through 66 to complete the engines mounted near the tail.
sections.fact: Many private jets keep their engines at the back of the plane, which helps keep the cabin quieter for passengers.

body.name: Paper Airplane
body.h1: Paper Airplane Dot to Dot — 56 Dots for a High-Flying Adventure
body.tagline: Fold, Fly, and Connect the Dots!
body.description: Connect 56 dots to reveal a classic paper airplane gliding through the air. This easy, beginner-friendly printable helps young children practise number sequencing, concentration, and steady pencil control.
body.fun_fact: A well-folded paper airplane can glide for a long time because its flat, angled wings push against the air just like a real plane's wings do.

dot_guide.heading: How to Solve the Paper Airplane Dot-to-Dot Puzzle
dot_guide.intro: This classic paper airplane is ready to soar! The 56-dot challenge is divided into four simple stages, perfect for little puzzlers just starting out. Find dot 1 and let's take off!
dot_guide.outro: Great flying—your paper airplane is ready to launch! Colour it in bright patterns, then try folding a real one to see it soar. Try the private jet dot to dot puzzle next for another easy, beginner-friendly adventure.

sections.title: The Pointed Nose
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 14 to draw the sharp, folded nose of the paper airplane.
sections.fact: A pointed nose helps a paper airplane slice through the air with less resistance, so it flies farther.

sections.title: The Folded Wings
sections.learn: Continue from dot 15 to dot 28 to shape the wide, folded paper wings.
sections.fact: The crisp fold lines on each wing keep them flat and stiff, which helps the plane glide smoothly instead of flopping around.

sections.title: The Body Crease
sections.learn: Follow dots 29 through 42 along the center crease that holds the paper airplane together.
sections.fact: The center crease acts like a spine, giving the paper airplane the strength to hold its shape while it flies.

sections.title: The Tail and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 43 through 56 to complete the tail edges at the back of the plane.
sections.fact: The back edges of the wings can be bent up slightly to help the paper airplane fly straighter instead of diving or spinning.

body.name: Glider
body.h1: Glider Dot to Dot — 67 Dots for a High-Flying Adventure
body.description: Connect 67 dots to reveal a graceful glider soaring silently on the wind. This easy, beginner-friendly printable helps children practise number sequencing, concentration, and steady pencil control.
body.fun_fact: Gliders have no engine at all—they use rising currents of warm air, called thermals, to stay aloft for hours at a time.

dot_guide.heading: How to Solve the Glider Dot-to-Dot Puzzle
dot_guide.intro: This quiet glider is riding the wind high above the clouds! The 67-dot challenge is divided into five easy stages, perfect for young puzzlers. Find dot 1 and catch the breeze!
dot_guide.outro: Fantastic soaring—your glider is riding the wind beautifully! Colour it in sky blues and whites, then add some fluffy clouds around it. Try the paper airplane dot to dot puzzle next for another easy, beginner-friendly adventure.

sections.title: The Nose and Cockpit
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 14 to draw the smooth, narrow nose and cockpit up front.
sections.fact: The pilot sits in a snug cockpit with a clear canopy, giving a wide view of the sky in every direction.

sections.title: The Long, Slender Wings
sections.learn: Continue from dot 15 to dot 28 to shape the glider's long, slim wings.
sections.fact: A glider's wings are much longer and thinner than an airplane's, which helps it catch rising air and fly farther without an engine.

sections.title: The Slim Fuselage
sections.learn: Follow dots 29 through 42 along the slender body connecting the wings to the tail.
sections.fact: Gliders are built as light and streamlined as possible, since every bit of extra weight makes it harder to stay in the air.

sections.title: The Tail Fin
sections.learn: Trace dots 43 through 55 to add the tall tail fin at the back of the glider.
sections.fact: The tail fin keeps the glider flying straight and steady as it rides the wind currents.

sections.title: The Wingtips and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 56 through 67 to complete the curved wingtips at the back of the glider.
sections.fact: Some gliders can stay in the air for hours, soaring on thermals without ever needing an engine to keep them going.
